Hayagrīvasaṁhitā
(‘scripture of हयग्रीव’)
------------------------------------------
The Pāñcarātra Āgamas are basic works of the cult of विष्णु-नारायण. The Hayagrīvasaṁhitā is one of the less known treatises of this group. It does not seem to have bean printed as yet. One of the manuscripts discovered has the following contents:
Pratiṣṭhākāṇḍa—42 paṭalas or chapters.
Saṁskārakāṇḍa—37 paṭalas.
Liṅgakāṇḍa—25 paṭalas.
Saurakāṇḍa—45 paṭalas.
The whole work deals with the rituals concerning the installation of images of various minor gods, methods of preparing the images as also various kinds of rituals themselves.
It is interesting to note that the third section—the Liṅgakāṇḍa—is śaivite in character.
See also PĀÑCARĀTRA ĀGAMAS.

Hayagrīva
(‘one with a horse’s head’)
------------------------------------------
Hayagrīva, the god with the head of a horse, is one of the minor incarnations of विष्णु.
Several stories are found in the Vedic and paurāṇic literature regarding this इन्चर्नतिओन्.
Yājñavalkya, the great sage, lost the यजुर्वेद as a result of the curse of वैशम्पायन, his teacher. He performed severe penance, praying to सूर्य, the Sun-god. Pleased by this, सूर्य appeared before him as a deity with the horse’s head and taught him the same Veda in another form. This section has come to be known as the Vājasaneyī Saṁhitā.
A demon, हयग्रीव by name, obtained several boons from the देवी and became a terror for the world. Since he had prayed that he could be killed only by another like him (i.e., with a horse’s head) the gods of हेअवेन् worked out a stratagem, by which विष्णु lost his original head and the Aśvinis (twin-gods, physicians of हेअवेन्) grafted a horse’s head. विष्णु, in this हयग्रीव form, killed the demon (Devībhāgavata 1.5).
According to another story, two demons मधु and कैटभ, had stolen the वेदस्. विष्णु took the form of हयग्रीव, killed them and recovered the वेदस्.
As per the story in the Śāntiparva (chapter 24) of the Mahābhārata, हयग्रीव was a noble king. Though he defeated his enemies, since he had not cultivated the friendship of others, he was ultimately killed by the same enemies. The lesson that व्यास taught to युधिष्ठिर by this story was that even mighty rulers must take the help of others.
Hayagrīva is the god of learning, akin to the goddess सरस्वती.
Iconographical works describe him as having a human form, with the head of a horse, possessing four or eight arms, carrying the various weapons and emblems of विष्णु.

Hayagrīva Upaniṣad
------------------------------------------
This minor Upaniṣad, classed among the Vaiṣṇava उपनिषद्स्, is assigned to the Atharvaveda. It has just 20 mantras, some being in verses and the rest in prose.
Nārada approaches ब्रह्मा, the Creator for the knowledge of ब्रह्मन् by which one destroys all sins and obtains eternal wealth. The Upaniṣad is a reply to this question and deals mainly with some mantras of Lord हयग्रीव by the repetition of which one can get all wealth, wealth of knowledge and wisdom.
At first, three long mantras are given. ब्रह्मा, अत्रि, Ravi, Savitṛ and भार्गव are the five ṛṣis or sages of these mantras. गायत्री, Triṣṭubh and Anuṣṭubh are the Vedic metres through which they are revealed. हयग्रीव is the deity. ‘Hlaum’ is the बीज or seed-letter. The mantras are capable of conferring happiness here and लिबेरतिओन् after death.
As a sample, one मन्त्र can be given here:
viśvottīrṇasvarūpāya
cinmayānandarūpiṇe ।
tubhyaṁ namo hayagrīva
vidyārājāya viṣṇave ॥
svāhā स्वाहा namaḥ ॥
The dhyānaśloka given next, describes the form of हयग्रीव to aid meditation. He has four arms holding the conch, the discus and the book in three hands and exhibiting the mahāmudrā (a pose of the hand) in the fourth. He is bright like the full-मोओन्.
This is followed by some more mantras of 29 letters, 34 letters, one letter (‘hlaum’) and 16 letters, their use for getting certain desires fulfilled and an explanation as to how these mantras reflect the meaning of the mahāvākyās (‘great sentences’ of Vedānta like tat tvam asi).
The work ends with a phalaśruti or eulogy, of the knowledge contained here which, when repeated (especially on an एकादशी day), confers greatness (mahā-puruṣatva).
